findings.title: Second downsize definition overrides the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The new self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 replaces the self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) defined at line 145. Existing callers that pass separate width and height values will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments), breaking thumbnail/avatar downsizing paths that use the original signature.

findings.title: Animated GIF detection fails for extensionless upload tempfiles
findings.body: Upload and downloaded-file tempfiles normally have paths without a .gif extension. OptimizedImage.optimize selects its animated instructions only when the source path matches /\.GIF$/i, so passing tempfile.path here never selects that path despite allow_animation being supplied. The normal downsize instructions use `#{from}[0]`, selecting only the first frame, so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened instead of being resized as an animation. The extensionless destination can also prevent ImageMagick from inferring the intended output format.

findings.title: Failed image conversions are retried blindly and then ignored
findings.body: The loop ignores the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails—for example for an unsupported/corrupt image or an SVG matched by FileHelper.is_image?—it invokes the same failing conversion up to five times and then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the original oversized file. This wastes external-process work and makes the automatic-downsizing feature fail opaquely instead of falling back or reporting the conversion failure.

findings.title: Hardcoded 10 MB client limit ignores configured image and attachment limits
findings.body: Replacing Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] with a fixed 10 MB breaks sites whose configured limits differ: attachments or images allowed above 10 MB by an administrator are rejected client-side, while files above a lower configured limit pass client validation and fail later on the server. The hardcoded value in the 413 handler at line 246 likewise reports 10 MB even when the server limit that produced the rejection is different.

findings.title: URL download limit is changed to a fixed 10 MB for every upload type
findings.body: The API URL-download cap no longer uses SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb and is fixed at 10 megabytes regardless of whether the upload is an image or an attachment. This rejects remotely fetched files that the site configuration would allow above 10 MB, and it downloads non-image attachments up to 10 MB even when the applicable configured limit is lower; those attachments cannot be downsized and are only rejected after the transfer.
